paper_metadata.title: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Portfolio Selection: A Comparative Study with Classical Markowitz Optimization

summary: The paper studies a 6-asset portfolio-selection QUBO solved with QAOA at depths p=1 and p=2 on a Qiskit Aer statevector simulator using 1024 shots. Reported QUBO costs are -17.740 for QAOA p=1, -17.630 for QAOA p=2, and -17.745 for the exact classical QUBO solver, so the classical method is slightly better and no quantum advantage is shown.

experiments.description: QAOA applied to a 6-asset discrete portfolio selection QUBO, evaluated at depths p=1 and p=2 on a Qiskit simulator and compared against an exact classical QUBO solver baseline.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA for QUBO/Ising portfolio optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary asset-selection variable; 6 binary variables mapped to 6 qubits via xi = (1 - Zi)/2
problem_formulation.objective_function: Cost(x) = -\u2211_i \u03bc_i x_i + \u03bb \u2211_{i,j} \u03a3_ij x_i x_j + penalty terms
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty terms for cardinality / portfolio-size / budget violations
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_C = \u2211_i h_i Z_i + \u2211_{i<j} J_ij Z_i Z_j + constant

problem_instance.description: Small synthetic discrete portfolio selection instance

dataset_specification.description: synthetically generated expected returns and covariance matrix; no real tickers or date range reported

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: synthetic generation of \u03bc_i and \u03a3_ij to create a controlled, reproducible small instance
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: single reported implementation comparing QAOA p=1, QAOA p=2, and exact classical QUBO solution; no repeated-run statistics reported

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: bitstring selection and comparison of expected return, variance, and QUBO cost

speedup_claims.conditions: small 6-asset instance on a simulator; paper explicitly states no practical advantage or quantum speedup is demonstrated
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic complexity comparison or runtime benchmark is reported; results are pedagogical and exploratory.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not established; paper uses a 6-qubit noiseless simulator with 1024 shots and no runtime benchmark or scaling study.
limiting_factors: Only a 6-asset toy instance is studied
Execution is on a classical simulator, not quantum hardware
No demonstrated speedup or runtime advantage
Classical exact QUBO solver matches or slightly outperforms QAOA on reported costs
No asymptotic complexity or crossover analysis is provided

notes: hardware.type reported as Qiskit aer simulator (statevector) in the experimental setup; provider set to IBM because Qiskit is an IBM framework, but no specific IBM device is used.
circuit_depth recorded as [1,2] because the paper evaluates QAOA at p=1 and p=2.
num_variational_params inferred as [2,4] from 2p parameters for p=1 and p=2.
